steps.line: The pigeons are organised. They meet every morning by {next}, I've seen them nodding. Go and listen in, quietly, act like a bench.
A tiny memo: 'Agenda. 1, crumbs. 2, more crumbs. 3, that man with the notebook.' Show it to Gus's sister at {next}.
Gus thinks it's a plot. What's item three on the pigeons' agenda?
steps.wrong: Read the memo again, love. Number three is the interesting one.
steps.right: Ha! They're watching him because he feeds them. Tell him to meet me at {next} with a bag of seeds.

steps.line: So the pigeons aren't plotting, they're a fan club, and I'm the celebrity. Honestly that's nicer. Have some seeds, they'll want to meet you too.
Darling! I sang the Sleepwell Mattress jingle in 1987. It's time for my comeback. My old manager Benny hangs about near {next}, fetch him.
Dolores wants a comeback? She'll need her lucky sequin. It popped off during a high note at {next} in '94 and she's never sung since.
Still sparkly after thirty years. Benny says the comeback show is at {next}, and she'll need an audience, so that's you.
Quick, before I go on: what did I sing in 1987? I want to open with it.
steps.wrong: Close, darling, but it was about a bed. Think comfort.
steps.right: Sleep well, sleep deep! Oh, it still works. Meet me at {next} after, for the encore.

steps.line: Four people clapped and one dog howled along. Best show of my career. Take this, every star should own a record.
Welcome, seekers. Step one: breathe. Step two: go where the water sits very still and thinks about life. You'll know it.
Very calm. A note on a post says 'Step three: eat a snack. Calm is easier with a snack.' The snacks are at {next}.
Brook sent you? He's sent forty people today and he's never once finished his own steps. He's stuck on step five, over at {next}.
I'm stuck. Remind me, what was step three? I wrote it at four in the morning.
steps.wrong: No, that was step two. Step three was tastier.
steps.right: A snack! That's why I'm stuck, I skipped it. Let's do step seven together at {next}.

steps.line: Step seven: tell someone they did well today. You did well today. That's the whole book, honestly. Here, it's a bit thin.
My self-stirring teacup is nearly done! It stirs, and it rings when the tea's ready. My old teacher at {next} kept my blueprints.
Nadia's blueprints are in one of these drawers. Which one, do you think?
steps.wrong: She was a very literal student. Think about what she's building.
steps.right: Tea Things, of course. It says she left the parts around town. Her brother Pip at {next} will send you off.

steps.line: That's all three! The bell goes on top, obviously, that's the ringing bit. Take them to Nadia at {next}.
It stirs! It rings! It also spun the tea onto the ceiling, but that's a version two problem. Have the bell, I've got spares.

hunt.line: Nadia hides things like a squirrel hides nuts. Go and find {items}, then come back here.

steps.line: Clive Pennywhistle has spotted 312 birds this year. I have 311. Someone saw a rare blue-tailed warbler near {next}. Go, quietly!
A bright blue feather, the warbler was here! A dog walker says it flew up to the spot where you can see the whole town at once.

steps.hint: Where the whole town fits in view
steps.line: There it is, singing! And there's Clive, also watching it, with very fancy binoculars. He waves you over to {next}.
Harriet sent you? Then prove you saw it. What colour was its tail?
steps.wrong: Hmm, that's not what I saw. Think about that feather.
steps.right: Blue. You're real witnesses. Let's tell Harriet together at {next}. It's a tie, and a tie means cake.

steps.line: 312 each! Clive and I have agreed to share the title, and a bench. Here, a little something for my favourite spotters.
Gather round! Tonight's tour has three stops. The first is {next}, where a ghost once returned a library book 80 years late.
That ghost was my grandad, he just ran very late. Mortimer's next story is where you cross the water and don't get wet.
Mortimer says a ghost here whistles at midnight. It's the wind in a gap, but he's selling whistles. His last stop is {next}.
Final question for my brave group: what did the library ghost really bring back?
steps.wrong: Spooky guess, but no. Think back to the very first stop.
steps.right: Correct! Not spooky, just very overdue. For the grand finale, follow me to {next}. Bring your courage, or a snack.

steps.line: And here, at last, a real ghost. She's lovely, she just wants someone to say goodnight to. Say goodnight, everyone.
I'm retiring, and I want one last show. Trouble is, my props are everywhere. My wand was last seen near {next}.
His wand! It's a stick with a ribbon on it, honestly. The tag says 'If found, return to Lottie at {next}.'
Coin, cards, ribbon and wand. That's the whole act. He's waiting at {next}, pretending he isn't nervous.
Is this your card? It is? After fifty years it finally worked! Thank you. Every good assistant gets cake.

hunt.line: I was his assistant for thirty years, he sheds props like a dog sheds fur. Bring back {items}.

steps.npc: A man in a fake moustache
steps.line: Shh. I'm Basil Thorne, food critic, in disguise. Please taste the town for me, I'm too recognisable. Start at {next}.
Is that Basil in a moustache? Bless him. Tell him our scones are made with honey, his favourite. Then try the soup at {next}.
Soup today is pumpkin, it's always pumpkin. Basil once wrote it was orange in spirit. He's hiding behind a newspaper at {next}.
Report! Which place uses honey, my favourite thing in the world?
steps.wrong: No, that was the pumpkin soup. Think about what Maria told you.
steps.right: Honey scones! Five stars. Let me peel off this moustache and meet you at {next}.

steps.line: My review: this town is delicious, and very kind to strangers in moustaches. Here, share this, critic's orders.

stories.title: Not From Around Here, or Now

steps.line: Greetings from the year 2186! My time machine needs a part only found in your era: a decent cup of tea. Try {next}.
Him again? He's been from the future every Tuesday since 1998. Here's his tea. He dropped his watch near {next}, by the way.
A pocket watch, set exactly one hour fast. Engraved: 'To Tock, who is always early.' He's waiting at {next}.
My chronometer! Tell me, is it set to the past, the present or the future?
steps.wrong: Look again, it's ahead of everyone else's.
steps.right: The future! Only an hour, but still. I am a time traveller, just a slow one. Walk with me to {next}.

steps.line: We all travel through time, one minute per minute, I'm just a bit ahead. Keep a clock of your own, so you're never late either.
I'm the number one fan of The Soggy Biscuits, who split up in 2003 over a sandwich. I want them back together! The drummer works at {next}.
A reunion? Only if they've forgiven me. Do you even know what we argued about?
steps.wrong: Kiki tells everyone the story. Think about lunch.
steps.right: A sandwich. Ham, I think. It's silly now. Our singer teaches at {next}, go ask her.

steps.line: Pick, lyrics and drumsticks, we're a band again. Tell Kiki to bring everyone to {next}, and maybe a sandwich to share.
They're playing! All four of them! And they're sharing a sandwich on stage! This is the best day of my life.

hunt.line: If we're doing this, we need our old gear. It's scattered all over town. Fetch {items}.

steps.line: Three nights running, lights over the park! Blinking, gliding, very un-plane-like. A witness saw them from {next}, let's interview him.
Green and red lights, blinking, low over the trees around nine. And a buzzing, like a very small bee with a very big job. Look around {next}.
A tiny metal bit with a screw hole. Alien technology? Orla wants it shown to someone who knows machines, at {next}.
Interesting part. And Frank said the lights were what colours?
steps.wrong: That's not what Frank told you. Think back.
steps.right: Green and red, blinking. That rings a bell, but I won't spoil it. Tell Orla, she's at {next}.

steps.line: Green and red, buzzing, and a metal part! The evidence is piling up. Same time next week, partners. Glow in the dark, so they can find us.
Big news, the lights came back and something landed! Well, bumped into a hedge. Near {next}. Bring notebooks.
A note: 'Practice H, then A, then P, then P...' Orla thinks it's an alien alphabet. A gardener at {next} might have seen something.
It bumped my roses and said sorry in a tiny old man voice, I think. Then it buzzed up toward the spot with the best view of town.

steps.hint: Where you can see it all
steps.line: From up here: a blinking light in a window nearby, practising little loops. Orla is beside herself. Report to her at {next}.
The note said H, A, P, P. What do you think it's trying to spell?
steps.wrong: Check the letters on the note again, the first four.
steps.right: HAPPY! The aliens are happy! Or someone is. Next week, we find out who. Meet me at {next}.

steps.line: A window, a note and a happy alien. One more night and we'll know everything. Take a cookie, it might be a long stakeout.
Tonight we meet the pilot. Remember: green and red lights, spelling HAPP-something. The blinking window is by {next}. Knock politely, like ambassadors.
Lights? Blinking? Go on then, what colours were they, if you're so sure it's me?
steps.wrong: Nope, not mine. Orla told you the colours, didn't she?
steps.right: Fine, it's me! It's my toy plane with fairy lights, spelling HAPPY 50TH for my wife. Help? My grandson's at {next}.

steps.line: All fixed! Grandad's launching from {next}, and Gran's coming out to look at the stars. Shh, act casual.
HAPPY 50TH, in green and red, right across the sky. It wasn't aliens. It was better. I'm still keeping my tinfoil hat, though.

hunt.line: Grandad's plane has been dropping bits all week. Find {items} and it'll fly perfectly.

steps.line: I'm shooting a tiny film about a lost umbrella and I need extras! Wardrobe is at {next}, tell them Juno sent you.
Extras for Juno? Here's the brief: walk past slowly and look mildly surprised. That's it, that's the acting. Scene one is at {next}.
Places, everyone! Remind me what wardrobe told you. How do my extras walk?
steps.wrong: Lovely energy, but wardrobe gave you the brief. Think back.
steps.right: Perfectly surprised, print it! Oh no, page one of my script blew away, toward {next}.

steps.line: Page one, damp but readable: 'Scene: an umbrella is lost.' Very meta. Take it back to Juno at {next}.
Day one, done. You were the best mildly surprised people I've ever filmed. Here's your extra's pay, I'm afraid it's bread.
Big scene today, but my lead Harold has stage fright and forgot his only line. The writer, Priya, is at {next}. Ask her.
His line is 'At last, it's stopped raining.' Five words, he's practised since March. He's hiding at {next}, poor dear.
I can't remember it. Something about the weather? Which one is it?
steps.wrong: No, that's not it. Priya said it had rain in it.
steps.right: That's it! I can do this. But the crew lost their gear, and the gaffer at {next} needs a hand.

steps.line: All here! Harold's ready, and Juno is shouting action at {next}. Go, go, quietly!
He said it! Five words, perfect, and then he bowed, which wasn't in the script. I kept it. Here, a little wrap gift.

hunt.line: Gear everywhere, like a parade went through. Find {items} and we can roll.

steps.line: The film's done! Eleven minutes, three of them are the umbrella. The premiere's tonight, but I forgot posters. Lenny prints things at {next}.
Posters, sure, but which title? Her napkin says The Lost Umbrella, Wet Tuesday and Brolly, and the last two are crossed out. Ask Harold at {next}.
I'm the star and nobody told me the title. Which one made the cut?
steps.wrong: That one's crossed out, Lenny said so.
steps.right: The Lost Umbrella. Classic. Now Juno wants to screen it at one of the town's public buildings, go find one.

steps.line: A big blank wall, perfect for a screen. Juno says to gather the whole cast at {next} for the red carpet.
Eleven minutes, and everyone clapped for all of them. Even the umbrella took a bow. Thank you, my wonderful extras. Party time!
(Marcel holds up a card: 'Silent for 30 years. My granddaughter graduates today. Help me pick my first word.' He points at {next}.)
Grandpa wants to talk? He mimed proud at me every day since I was six, chest out, thumbs up. His old partner is at {next}.
(Sue mimes being stuck in a box, steps out, and hands you a note: 'He practised one word in the mirror for years. It starts with P. He's at {next}.')
(Marcel holds up three cards and raises his eyebrows very high. Which should be his first word?)
steps.wrong: (Marcel shakes his head kindly, mimes a small girl, then a thumbs up. Think of Amelie.)
steps.right: (Marcel nods, takes a huge breath, and marches you toward {next}, chest out, thumbs up.)

steps.line: Proud. (He said it! His voice is very squeaky. Amelie is crying. Marcel mimes handing you a flower, then really does.)
I'm the town's unofficial bench inspector. Forty years, 212 benches. Today, the bench by {next}. Sit on it, report back, be honest.
A plaque fell off the bench: 'For Walter, who likes the view and a good sandwich.' Ida's friend Pearl at {next} might know Walter.
Walter! Cheese and pickle every lunch for twenty years. Ida's sweet on him, she just rated him four stars. He's feeding ducks by {next}.
Ida sent you? What does my plaque say I like, besides the view?
steps.wrong: Not quite, have another look at that plaque.
steps.right: A good sandwich, yes. Tell Ida I'll bring two to {next}, and that it's a five star bench now.

steps.line: He's bringing two sandwiches? Well. That bench is five stars, and maybe Walter too. Here, make a sign for the next good bench you find.
This stick finds water, it's never wrong, mostly. Today it's twitching toward somewhere wet where the ducks hang about. Follow the stick!
Water! Doug is thrilled. Now the stick twitches again and he says it means lost and shiny. Search around {next}.
A gold ring in the grass, engraved 'D and M, 1979'. Doug's wife Marion is at {next}, she's been hoping for this.
Our ring! Doug lost it dowsing last spring. Go on, what's engraved inside?
steps.wrong: Ha! No, look again, it's our initials.
steps.right: D and M. Let's give the stick the credit, he'll love that. Find Doug at {next}, I'm right behind you.

steps.line: My ring! The stick did it! (Marion winks at you.) Here, every dowser needs a stick. Don't let it go to your head.
I am Madame Woof, pet psychic. A little dog called Pickle is missing, and I sense... bread. A strong smell of bread. Try {next}.
Pickle? Scruffy little thing, one ear up? He had his usual crust, then trotted off toward {next}, very pleased with himself.
A tag: 'PICKLE. If found, he's probably nearby being adored.' Madame Woof is at {next}, having a vision.
My visions are cloudy. Remind my spirit guides, what does Pickle look like?
steps.wrong: The spirits say no. What did the baker tell you?
steps.right: Scruffy, one ear up. I see him! He's being adored by {next}. Go!

steps.line: Pickle! Exactly where my visions said, roughly. Fine, the baker helped. But I felt it in my heart. Good dog.
I'm campaigning to make Mittens the cat our honorary mayor. We need signatures! Start with the regulars at {next}.
Mittens? She naps on my windowsill every day at noon, like clockwork. Of course I'll sign. The kids at {next} adore her too.
We drew forty posters. Mittens sat on one and licked another, which counts as yes. Reggie's practising his speech at {next}.
One last fact for my speech: when does Mittens nap at Nora's window?
steps.wrong: Nora told you, think lunchtime.
steps.right: Noon! A mayor with a schedule. The ceremony's at {next}, bring everyone.

steps.line: By the power of 300 signatures and one licked poster, I give you Mayor Mittens! She's asleep. Very mayoral.
I buried a time capsule in 1985 and wrote the clues in rhyme so I'd remember. I don't. Clue one: start where the whole town waits for a ride.

steps.hint: Where the town waits for a ride
steps.line: Clue two, scratched on a post: 'Next, where the town buys its food.' Agatha admits she was very hungry in 1985.
The owner remembers! 'Dr. Penn bought a bun and walked off with a shovel.' She went toward {next}.
A scrap of map with an X: 'Under the third tree from the left, you clever thing.' Take it to Agatha at {next}.
The third tree! Let's open it. My 1985 self left a note: 'Hope you found this, you clever thing.' I did, with help.
I've attempted 41 world records and failed all 41. Today: most hellos in one afternoon! The first hello is at {next}. Bring a smile.
A hello record? Lovely. Hello! That's one. Barry's tally keeper is waiting at {next}, he'll want the count.
For the certificate, how many records has Barry failed before today?
steps.wrong: Less lucky than that, sadly. Barry told you himself.
steps.right: Forty-one. This could be his first win! Barry's waiting at {next} with the next bit.

steps.line: Three neighbours, three hellos, all proven! The official judge, my mum, is at {next}.
Most hellos in one afternoon, a record! Nobody else tried, but it counts. Barry's first win. Here, it's a medal, roughly.

hunt.line: The judges need proof. Each neighbour left a hello token. Collect {items}.

steps.line: My garden gnomes go on holiday every summer and send postcards. Three haven't come home this year. The last postcard came from near {next}.
Tiny writing: 'Having a lovely time. Back soon. P.S. The other two are with Kofi.' Kofi is at {next}.
Souvenirs found, and all three gnomes asleep in my shed. Carry them home to Mrs. Thistle at {next}.
All home! And look at all the postcards from their travels. Next year, I'm going with them.

hunt.line: Those gnomes left souvenirs all over town, terrible tourists. Collect {items}.

steps.line: Someone's been knitting cosy jumpers for lamp posts all over town. It's me. I'm 84. Help me with my biggest project? Start at {next}.
Granny Purl? She knitted my teapot a hat. She'll need more wool, she hides a stash near {next} so her daughter won't find it.
A tin of wool, every colour, and a note: 'Do not tell Linda.' Linda, her daughter, is at {next}. Act natural.
Mum's knitting again, isn't she? Be honest. What did she knit for Hal's teapot?
steps.wrong: No, Hal told you. Think about what keeps your head warm.
steps.right: A hat. Of course. Tell her I'm not cross, I'm proud, and I'll meet you both at {next}.

steps.line: Linda's helping? Then the big jumper will be done by Friday. Take this, everyone in the knitting club gets some.
